citations.desc: Attending veterinarian and adequate veterinary care (dealers and exhibitors).
citations.narrative:
The facility did not perform complete daily observations of all animals to adequately assess their health and well being.
During examination of a fifteen year old black and white male poodle named “Rio” (microchip# 985113007469460), the
APHIS official noted a moderate amount of hardened brown material adhered to most of the dog’s upper teeth. The gums
were red and had receded from the surface of several upper molars, premolars, and canines. No odor was detected
during the oral exam, and no abnormal behavior was observed during the distance evaluation. The dog appeared to be in
good body condition.
The facility representative reported that he had not previously noticed this level of tartar prior to the inspection. The
licensee stated that dental procedures are typically performed at the end of the travel fair season. The lack of timely
dental care can lead to conditions such as dental disease that may cause pain and discomfort and can result in additional
health complications.
Exhibitors shall establish and maintain program of adequate veterinary care that include daily observation of all animals to
assess their health and well-being; Provided, however, That daily observation of animals may be accomplished by
someone other than the attending veterinarian; and Provided, further, That a mechanism of direct and frequent
communication is required so that timely and accurate information on problems of animal health, behavior, and well-being
is conveyed to the attending veterinarian. Correct by 10/8/2026.

A four year old female black Border Collie named “Nala” (microchip# 985113007470950) did not have continuous access
to potable water. During the inspection, Nala was housed inside the air conditioned trailer in her primary enclosure which
‑
did not contain a water source. When asked about the lack of water, the licensee stated that she tends to knock over or
chew on the water receptacle. He explained that he offers her water periodically as needed. Constant access to potable
water is necessary to ensure that dogs remain hydrated as needed throughout the day. The facility must ensure that all
dogs have continuous access to potable water, unless restricted by the attending veterinarian or except as provided in
3.17(a). Corrected at the time of inspection.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with a facility representative. he inspection was conducted at the North
Alabama State Fair in Muscle Shoals, AL.
You may appeal all or part of any inspection report by submitting a written statement contesting the findings—along with
any supporting documentation—to the Deputy Administrator. Appeals of routine, focused, or attempted inspections must
be received within 21 days of report issuance as shown by the signature line of this report.
Appeals may be sent by email to AnimalCare@usda.gov.
Appeals sent by mail should be addressed to:

APHIS Animal Care (AC)
U.S. Department of Agriculture
